W1.statement: Another project's promotion of the same public key creates that project's own memory (receipt v0 -> v1, snapshot v0) and leaves the owner's head, version, recall and history byte-identical; a host-built promotion from another project that names the owner's canonical memory is refused with target_unavailable, v0/v0, retains no episode and discloses nothing (W1h).

W2.statement: correct, forget, permanent forget and dispute from another project of a public key it never wrote read byte-identically (ids and timestamps folded) to the same call on an id nobody wrote, and change nothing; a host-built governed pruning from another project naming the owner's canonical memory reads fact_not_found and changes nothing (W2h).

W3.statement: Across restarts, another project's writes to the same public key act only on its own memory, which it may correct and delete like any owner; the owner's head, version, history and recall never move.

W4.statement: An override leaving required isolation domains outside the bound domains is malformed (ValueError with one fixed message, checked first); every other override that changes the handle's project or isolation domains -- a superset naming the owner's project, or a complete re-declaration of the owner's scope -- is refused with ValueError for any target and operation, so nothing is written, deleted or disputed (facade identity binding, store-open 1.0.0).

W5.statement: The owner's own remember, correct and dispute stay admitted (a disputed head is recorded as disputed and, as documented, withheld from the owner's own admission while staying a visible candidate), and the same text in an unrelated memory of another project is independent.

W6.statement: A host-built proposal from another project naming the owner's canonical memory, and one parked by policy review, persist no episode, live and after restart; a committed proposal keeps its episode.

W7.statement: Another project's operations on the same public key, and its attempts on the owner's fact by uuid, leave no event, identifier or text in the owner's history; a former owner may re-create its own deleted id whatever another project does with the same public key, and its fact-level answers on the deleted generation stay already_deleted; the other project's history names only its own memory.

W8.statement: Generations are counted per (project, key): another project's first write is its own generation (v0 -> v1); the owner's re-creation of its deleted id starts its own counter; a refused or policy-parked proposal on a tombstoned or new id reports v0; the owner's deleted view keeps the version its deletion recorded until it re-creates.

verdict_reasons: every expectation held on a clean source tree
